comment: Phase 7.9 hardening: Content Security Policy for the deployed frontend.
See implementation_phase_7.md §7.9.
default-src 'self': every resource must come from THIS origin unless a
more specific directive says otherwise.
script-src 'self': no inline <script> and no third-party JS. The vendored
@noble/post-quantum bundle (frontend/js/vendor/pqc.min.js) is served
from our own origin and is covered by 'self'.
connect-src 'self' wss://<cloud-run-host> https://<supabase-project>.supabase.co:
XHR/fetch/WebSocket can talk only to this origin, the Cloud Run backend
over TLS, and the Supabase Auth endpoint used by the Google Sign-In
redirect flow (the browser POSTs the code to Supabase, which returns the
session JWT). Replace both placeholders before deploy — a wildcard here
would defeat the point.
object-src 'none': no <object>/<embed>/<applet>. Nothing legitimate needs them.
base-uri 'none': the <base> tag cannot be injected to rewrite relative URLs.
frame-ancestors 'none': the site cannot be embedded in an iframe — the
operational answer to clickjacking, stronger than X-Frame-Options.
form-action 'self': a submitted form cannot POST to a third-party origin,
which is the classical CSRF exfil vector for form-based attacks.
REMEMBER TO REPLACE <cloud-run-host> WITH THE REAL BACKEND HOSTNAME.
A vercel deploy with this file unchanged will refuse to connect to any
backend at all, which is the correct fail-closed behaviour.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' wss://<cloud-run-host> https://<supabase-project>.supabase.co; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'
